QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Landscape and Types_12

question.text: Ms. Meera Krishnan, a sophisticated HNI, wants exposure to unlisted growth-stage Indian companies with a 7-year horizon, willing to accept illiquidity and a INR 1 crore minimum commitment for higher risk-adjusted returns. Among the channels discussed in the chapter, which is the MOST appropriate vehicle?

answer.text: Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) at INR 10 lakh minimum

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter describes AIFs as privately pooled vehicles collecting funds from sophisticated investors with a defined investment policy. Cat II AIFs invest primarily in unlisted equity and debt (PE/debt strategies) — exactly Ms. Krishnan's profile. MF units are liquid, listed-market instruments (wrong channel). SIF has a INR 10 lakh minimum but remains within the mutual-fund daily-NAV framework, unsuitable for 7-year illiquid unlisted-equity strategies. ULIP is an insurance-investment hybrid, unrelated. The Trap: (A) Mutual funds cannot take the illiquid unlisted concentration a growth PE strategy requires. (C) SIF was introduced by SEBI (Mutual Funds) Third Amendment 2024 with INR 10 lakh minimum, but it operates within MF infrastructure — not a PE vehicle. (D) ULIP is insurance, not a channel for unlisted-growth exposure. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests channel-matching to investor profile. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) treats it for listed-only mandates, so AIF is out of scope there. Manager's Pro-Tip: When pitching a Cat II growth fund to HNI LPs, contrast it explicitly with PMS and SIF in your PPM's 'Why AIF' section: minimum ticket, liquidity profile, taxation pass-through (115UB), and regulatory wrapper. This up-front differentiation reduces LP confusion later.
